To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TVNZ is disproportionately dependent on commercial revenues to fund programming initiatives; the Treasury is not bound by the TVNZ Charter and is able to use its power as shareholder to demand dividends; and the Ministry for Culture & Heritage is constrained by a lack of funding to support its role in the charter process and is unable to provide sufficient funding to TVNZ for its charter obligations.
the introduction of the charter in 2003 has not significantly altered the funding structure of TVNZ.
the introduction of the TVN charter has been successful in providing public services, but that the funding mechanism is problematic because it is not sufficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the politics of the TVNZ Charter, and the way in which different institutional agents have negotiated the charter's funding mechanism.
the ways in which the political economy of broadcasting is constituted and reconstituted by different agents in different institutional contexts.
how the political economy of broadcasting is constituted by, and constitutive of, the politics of funding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TVNZ Charter is a failure.

the government's decision to fund the charter through the Ministry of Culture was not a political strategy to reduce the broadcaster's dependence on commercial revenue, but a pragmatic response to the government's desire for greater control over charter funding.
the government is committed to public service broadcasting, but not at the expense of commercial imperatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the government’s decision to fund charter initiatives was an attempt to reconcile the commercial and public service obligations of TVNZ, but it has been undermined by the Treasury’s insistence on dividend payments.
the government is not as committed to the public broadcasting charter as it claims.
the government has failed in its attempt to create a public service broadcasting model in New Zealand.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Treasury's role in the funding of charter programming has been to maintain a level of commercial performance in TVNZ that has allowed it to remain profitable and to continue to pay dividends to the government.
the TVNZ charter has not delivered the public service broadcasting (PSB) that was promised.
, despite a range of institutional agents and structures, the Treasury has been able to retain control over funding mechanisms and policy decisions in the broadcasting sector.
